Forecast Discussion

High pressure settles directly over the mountains today, then drifts north of us Tuesday. Clear, calm nights bring frost to the valleys, and afternoons warm under full sun. The dry air exaggerates the valley-to-ridgetop swing.

Another high builds over New England Wednesday. A weak southeasterly flow around its southern side adds clouds and knocks afternoon temperatures down a few degrees for a day. The high slides off the coast Thursday, and a return flow brings gradually warmer afternoons Thursday and Friday.

Clouds thicken Saturday ahead of a system that stays west of us through Halloween. Trick-or-treating remains dry. I cannot rule out spotty light rain late Saturday night, and periods of light rain are possible Sunday as moisture rides up and over cooler air near the surface. The timing of the transition to a wetter pattern early next week is uncertain now but will come into focus as we get closer.
